items.title: Eliminating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference with Integer-Only Arithmetic (15 minute read)
items.snippet: A floating-point number stores a fixed number of significant digits and a separate exponent. When two numbers with very different exponents are added, the small one has to be shifted to line up with the big one, and the digits that fall off on the end are gone. That means that (a+b)+c is not always equal to a+(b+c). This post looks at what happens when integer addition, which is exact, is used.

items.title: Everyone is learning the wrong lesson from Hugging Face (9 minute read)

People see it as an example of how AI could be used to break into critical infrastructure and cause enormous damage.
